Verified false positive by grepping every other `limit`-style MCP param in this file (lines 5630, 5838, 6021): all three pre-existing sibling read tools use plain param_int for `limit` too. param_int_strict's own doc comment scopes it to date-range-affecting params reviewed individually, not a blanket requirement. trigger: An operator or SIEM engineer reads docs/user-manual/audit-log.md's 'Logged actions' table (the doc's own framing: 'The following actions are recorded automatically') expecting it to be the complete audit-verb catalog for SOC 2 evidence / detection-rule authoring
summary: This diff mints a brand-new audit verb, preflight.run.view (GET /api/v1/preflight/runs' service-scoped-token denial), and adds a second emitter (the new GET /api/v1/deployments/preview route) of the pre-existing deployment.config.view verb - neither is reflected in audit-log.md's per-verb table, even though the sibling verbs in the exact same family (preflight.run, preflight.run.delete, deployment.config.view's existing row, deployment.advance, deployment.delete) are all documented there in comparable per-verb detail. docs/user-manual/preflight.md and rest-api.md (both touched by this diff) correctly describe the new verb at the route level, but audit-log.md - the canonical, SOC-2-framed action registry ('the audit log is the SOC 2 evidence chain') and explicitly in scope of Gate 2 docs-writer review item 5 ('any audit action table... the REST/store/plugin API contract touches') - was not updated. Does not conceal a breaking change, a data-loss risk, a migration step, or an irreversible operation, and does not misstate any EXISTING behavior (pure omission of a new entry, not a contradiction) - stays MEDIUM, not HIGH, per the I7 rule.
classification: wording/completeness (docs-writer WORDING+coverage domain, not a truth contradiction)
waiver_rationale: Not BLOCKING per the derived band (MEDIUM/SHOULD). Not filed as a GitHub issue this session per an explicit session-wide no-gh-mutations rule (read-only gh issue view/list only); dedupe-searched first (gh issue list --search "audit-log.md verb" surfaced #3391/#2535/#488 as thematically related audit-verb-documentation-completeness gaps in OTHER verbs, none a duplicate of preflight.run.view specifically). Recommended: file as a governance-deferred/task/P2 issue adding the missing row(s).

trigger: A transient PreflightRunStore Postgres fault (pool_.try_acquire_for(kReadTimeout) exhausted, or exec_params returning a non-PGRES_TUPLES_OK status) during list_runs() reached from the new GET /api/v1/preflight/runs REST route and the list_preflight_runs MCP tool
summary: list_runs() returned an empty vector uniformly for 'not open', 'pool lease timeout', AND 'query execution error', collapsing a store-level fault into the SAME response as a genuinely-empty saved-runs rail. The pre-existing HTML-fragment consumer (/fragments/auto) already carried this same masking, deliberately (preflight_run_store.hpp header: 'fail-soft... degrades to an honest note') - but that rationale does not transfer to a machine-readable 200 {"data":[]} JSON body with no note attached: a caller (especially an agentic one) cannot tell 'you have zero runs' from 'we could not ask', and correctly derives I3 (wrong result presented as correct) rather than I8 - initially misjudged as I8 and set aside as non-blocking, corrected on advisor review before commit. EXPOSURE E5 (rare environmental condition) does not cap the band (only E6, proof of production-unreachability, would - not available), so I3+E5/E3 derives HIGH == BLOCKING.
classification: truth (store-behavior claim). Pre-fix defect established by reading get_run/list_runs source and naming the exact branch (res.status()!=PGRES_TUPLES_OK||PQntuples()==0 -> nullopt; !lease -> empty/nullopt) - epistemic_status 'likely', NOT 'verified': no red test was run against the pre-fix code to directly observe the 200-empty response (correcting an earlier overclaim in this same field caught on advisor review before finalizing the report). Post-fix behavior (503/kInternalError) IS verified, by the new pool-starvation tests added in the fix commit, which pass green.

trigger: Same transient-fault class as G4036-UP1a but via get_run() reached from the new GET /api/v1/deployments/preview REST route and the get_deployment_preview MCP tool
summary: get_run() returned std::nullopt uniformly for 'not open'/'pool lease timeout'/'query execution error' AND for a genuine miss/not-yours - all four collapse to the SAME 404 (REST) / kInvalidParams (MCP). Lower severity than G4036-UP1a: 404 was ALREADY ambiguous by design (not-found vs not-yours, per the store's own doc comment - closes the existence oracle), so a third meaning on a rare store fault is a smaller behavioural change than list_runs' 200-vs-503 case, and stays I8 (the store fault reads as an already-overloaded permanent classification, not a fabricated 'the data says X' claim) - precedent: issue #3527 Gap 3, the identical defect class in ExecutionTracker::get_execution, filed as a plain 'bug' (not P1/blocking) following a prior /governance run on #1712. Separately, rest-api.md (this diff's own docs) publishes 'Pre-flight run store unavailable -> 503' for this route, which was only true for the unwired-pointer case before this fix - a doc/code contract mismatch per the SKILL's contract-tracing rule, resolved by making the code match the published claim rather than narrowing the doc.
classification: truth (store-behavior claim + doc-vs-code contract check). Pre-fix defect established by reading source and rest-api.md and naming the exact branch - epistemic_status 'likely', NOT 'verified' (no red test observed the pre-fix 404 on a store fault; correcting an earlier overclaim in this field caught on advisor review). Post-fix behavior IS verified by the new pool-starvation tests added in the fix commit.
waiver_rationale: Not BLOCKING on its own derivation (I8/MEDIUM, matching #3527's non-blocking disposition for the identical pattern) - fixed anyway, bundled into the same commit as G4036-UP1a, because get_run_checked already existed for that fix and applying it symmetrically to get_run closed the rest-api.md 503-contract gap for this route too at near-zero incremental cost.
